dataset: Camp Fire 2018 de-identified ground record: NIST 911, radio-log, rescue and timeline rows
licence: NIST technical notes are US government works (public domain in the US); cite NIST TN 2252 and TN 2252sup.
time_conversion: at = source clock time on the source date + 8 h; source rows are at 1-minute resolution
coordinate_precision: rounded to 3 decimal places (about 100 m), or 2 (about 1 km) for rows naming a residential street; null when absent or when one quote is listed at several points
interpretation: Rows are NIST's retrospective transcription of recordings and interviews, not a CAD export, and cover a sample of calls. 'reported' rows are Table A-2 observations whose Info. Source is a 911 call or the radio log; 'reconstructed' rows come from NIST summary tables (K-1, main Tables 10 and 13). time_precision 'approximate' marks a non-zero observation window, a time range (start time kept) or a summary-table time. Table K-1 gives clock times only and is sorted chronologically, so rows after the 23:30 row whose times run backwards are dated 11/9. K-1 times are each event's first datapoint.
de_identification: No source free text, names, house numbers, addresses, ages or medical details are kept. summary is a template of channel, category and road name; category comes from keyword rules in the generator; text_sha12 is a 12-hex SHA-256 prefix of the whitespace-normalized source row text, kept only to merge duplicate quotes of one observation. road_name is limited to the MAIN_ROADS allow-list in the generator (main roads, arterials, three collectors and the state highways); any other road is null. When a row names a road outside that list (a residential street), its point is rounded to 2 decimals (about 1 km) instead of 3.
